handoff: Blocking F1: observe reads the work tree, not the branch's HEAD tree, so if the files are deleted but the move commit never lands (crash, thrown or deferred commit), the move is never finished and the deletions ride into an unrelated later commit (D13, AC3). Minor F2-F4: bare catches, a story move deleting an uncopied slice copy, hand-built AC3 fixtures. Unit 1206, integration 726/6 skip, typecheck green.

findings.title: An interrupted removal is never finished: observe reads the work tree, not the branch
findings.detail:
`withBranchRecord` uses `treeRunStateFiles` (packages/store/src/run-state.ts:59), which runs readdirSync on the worktree. `moveRecord` (packages/cli/src/runtime/act/lifecycle.ts:363-367) deletes the files with `removeTreeRunState` before `act.commit`. There are three ways the deletions can be left without the move commit: (1) a crash between the two calls; (2) `git.commit` throws; (3) `act.commit` returns `deferred` because a merge or rebase started after decide's `busy` check (GIT_IN_PROGRESS). In case 3 moveRecord still returns ok: true. In every case the next tick finds no files, so there is no `branch_record` and no `move_record`. HEAD and the remote still hold runs/, and the unstaged deletions ride into the next boundary commit's `git add -A` (packages/adapters/src/git/index.ts:368), for example a step-done commit, with a different message and trailers. This breaks D13 ('Observe reports `runs/` still on a held unit's branch'; 'removes `runs/` from the branch in one commit "norn: move gh-9 run state off the branch"'; 'A machine dir that already holds the record with `runs/` still on the branch only finishes the removal') and AC3 ('when the next tick runs, then it only finishes the removal'). No data is lost, because the copies land first. The implementer's handoff names the gap.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Detect leftover run state from the branch, not only the work tree. For example, observe also lists the files under `<spec>/runs` in HEAD (git ls-tree, read-only) other than the handoffs, and reports `branch_record` with copy [] when HEAD has them and the work tree does not. Alternatively, have the act stage and commit the removal (git rm with a pathspec) as one step. Treat a `deferred` or failed commit as not done, so the next tick retries. Add an S1 test: delete the tree files without committing (the crash point), tick, and expect exactly one 'norn: move … off the branch' commit, pushed.

findings.title: Bare catches in treeRunStateFiles swallow every errno
findings.detail:
Both try/catch blocks (lines 65-68 and 76-80) catch every error and return as if there were no run state. An EACCES or ENOTDIR error therefore reports the branch's run state as absent, and the move never happens and nothing is surfaced. Elsewhere the code narrows the catch to ENOENT (snapshot.ts uses `isErrno(e, "ENOENT")`).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Catch only ENOENT (isErrno) and rethrow or surface anything else.

findings.title: The story's move removes a slice's story-branch copy that it did not copy
findings.detail:
When a slice is read from its own slice worktree's branch, the story's `copy` leaves that slice's folder out. `removeTreeRunState` still deletes the slice's folder under the story branch's runs/, and the `bad` check in decide (story.ts) looks only at the units in `copy`. If the slice branch's own copy fails validation (S2), the story branch's possibly good copy is deleted without being copied, while the slice is corrupt.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Make the story's move wait while any unit whose folder is under the story branch's runs/ has errors. Or remove only the folders that were copied or that the machine dir already holds.

findings.title: AC3 fixtures are partly built by hand, and one test asserts observe Facts
findings.detail:
Lines 150-151 and 171-175 build the fixtures with store `treeUnitRunStateDir`, a cpSync and a bad receipt written by hand. The spec asks for older-layout fixtures 'built with the harness's layout helpers, not by hand'. Lines 156-158 assert the internal `branch_record` fact through observeNow rather than what a person sees. Also, the `record.move_waits` rule (wait during a merge or rebase, H1) is covered only by a hand-built rule case, with no S1 test.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Extend `toBranchRunState` (or add a sibling harness helper) for the interrupted and broken variants, and assert only the outcome a person can see.

findings.title: The flat-record test is duplicated, and the loadStories flags are spread one by one
findings.detail:
`u.record !== undefined && normalRecord(u.record) === unitRecordPath(STORY_UNIT_DIR)` repeats the round.migrate condition at story.ts:115. In snapshot.ts, loadStories now repeats `...(opts.x ? { x: true } : {})` for four flags. Also, run-state.ts:64 uses an inline `import("node:fs").Dirent` type.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Extract `isFlatStoryRecord(uf)`, pass `opts` through, and import `Dirent` at the top.
